title: A Hollow for the Garden
premise: Kestrel Quintana copies prayers in a valley where magic cannot enter, believing her debt to the temple binds her more surely than any god. When the old gods wake and begin answering prayers directly, Kestrel learns the temple has been selling souls to the Hollow Court beneath the mountain—including her brother's, sold to settle their family's debt. To steal his soul back, she must cross the border where magic lives, discover that her own blood carries a dormant divine inheritance the gods have been quietly cultivating, and choose between the found family of the valley and the power that could save it. She succeeds in reclaiming her brother's soul, but only by shattering the temple's authority, accepting a fragment of divinity she can never fully control, and leaving the valley to guard the border she once believed was a wall.
about_author: Felix Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing abandoned parish records before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about bureaucracy, belief, and the people who fall through the cracks of both.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She transcribes prayers for illiterate petitioners in the temple scriptorium, hiding her literacy's true depth and her brother Wren's worsening silence since their parents died. Introduces the temple's debt system. Emotional beat: quiet resentment disguised as diligence.

chapters.title: Prayers That Answer Back
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A petitioner's prayer is answered aloud in the scriptorium—an impossibility in the magicless valley. The high scribe confiscates the prayer and warns Kestrel to forget it. Emotional beat: first crack in her worldview, fear sharpening into curiosity.

chapters.title: What Wren Won't Say
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Wren, a temple groundskeeper, is caught sleepwalking toward the mountain and speaking a language no one in the valley knows. Kestrel finds a contract bearing his name in the high scribe's locked cabinet. Emotional beat: protective fury and dawning betrayal.

chapters.title: The Debt of Blood
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She confronts the high scribe, who reveals their parents sold Wren's soul to the Hollow Court to settle their debts—and that Kestrel's own contract has a blank clause awaiting her signature. Emotional beat: the trap closes; she realizes invisibility was always someone else's design.

chapters.title: The Border of Unmaking
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Fleeing the temple, she reaches the valley's edge where magic cannot follow—and steps through anyway, expecting death. Instead the border parts around her like it knows her. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into the first taste of belonging to something larger.

chapters.title: Ash and Brindle
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. A disgraced hedge-witch turned smuggler, Ash finds Kestrel collapsed on the mountain road and recognizes the divine residue on her skin. Ash decides, cynically, that Kestrel is worth more alive. Emotional beat: transactional mercy hiding loneliness.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. They descend toward the mountain's under-city, where souls are traded like coin and the old gods' abandoned temples have been repurposed as markets. Kestrel sees Wren's soul-sigil for sale. Emotional beat: horror at a world that commodifies what the valley only pretends to protect.

chapters.title: A Name the Gods Remember
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. An old god's remnant, living in a cracked shrine, addresses Kestrel by a name she has never used—and explains her bloodline was bred by the valley's founders as a vessel for dormant divinity. Emotional beat: her identity as 'ordinary scribe' collapses; grief for a self that was a cage.

chapters.title: The Price of Passage
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash bargains with the Court's gatekeeper using a favor they swore never to spend, revealing their own sister's soul was sold here years ago. Kestrel witnesses Ash's buried grief. Emotional beat: found family begins forming through shared wounds, not shared history.

chapters.title: The Auction of Wren Quintana
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Wren's soul-sigil goes to auction. Kestrel bids the only currency the Court values: a promise of her own divine inheritance, sealed in blood. She wins—but the Court now holds a claim on her. Emotional beat: triumph laced with dread; she has traded one debt for a larger one.

chapters.title: What the Soul Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Reunited with his soul, Wren is neither whole nor grateful—he remembers the Court's whispers and the truth of their parents' death, which was no accident. Emotional beat: rescue does not restore; Kestrel must sit with a brother who is a stranger.

chapters.title: The Temple's Long Shadow
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Pursuers from the valley temple arrive, led by the high scribe, who offers to erase Kestrel's debts if she surrenders Wren and her inheritance to the temple's keeping. Emotional beat: temptation of the familiar; she refuses, and becomes a fugitive to her own home.

chapters.title: Ash's Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. The Court's agents come to collect Ash's blood-sealed promise. Ash chooses to burn their smuggler's network rather than betray Kestrel, losing everything but the two people beside them. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the truest form of choosing family.

chapters.title: The Hollow Throne
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The trio infiltrates the Court's heart and discovers the 'gods' beneath the mountain are the valley's founders—humans who consumed divinity and hollowed into hungering things, sustained by sold souls. Emotional beat: revelation that power's corruption is not a fall but a hunger chosen daily.

chapters.title: An Inheritance of Hunger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The hollow founders offer Kestrel her full inheritance: godhood, her brother's freedom, the valley's safety—forever, if she feeds them. She feels how easy it would be. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; she must refuse the very power she was made for.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Border
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel realizes the valley's magicless border was never protection—it was a pen, built to keep the founders' food supply docile. She begins unmaking it, letting magic flood the valley. Emotional beat: righteous destruction; the cost is that everyone she knew will wake to a changed world.

chapters.title: Storm Over the Valley
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Magic returns to the valley in a storm of answered prayers and old debts called due. The temple's authority shatters as its lies are made visible. Ash and Wren hold the border while Kestrel faces the founders. Emotional beat: chaos as liberation, fear as courage.

chapters.title: A Hollow for the Garden
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Climax. Kestrel offers the founders not her godhood but the one thing they cannot take: a willing, unforced fragment of herself—divinity given, not seized. Given freely, it unmakes their hunger; taken by force, it would have completed it. Emotional beat: power's corruption answered by gift; the founders dissolve into the mountain's roots.

chapters.title: Debts Written in Water
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren, whole for the first time, chooses to stay at the mountain as a warden of the Court's remnants rather than return to the valley. Emotional beat: bittersweet separation; found family means letting people choose their own shape.

chapters.title: The Scribe of the Border
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The valley rebuilds without the temple's ledgers. Kestrel is asked to lead and declines, taking instead the post no one wants: scribe of the open border, recording what crosses and what doesn't. Emotional beat: identity remade on her own terms—visible, chosen, ordinary in the ways that matter.

chapters.title: What Ash Kept
chapters.summary: Ash's POV. Ash, unexpectedly offered a place in the valley, almost leaves out of habit—then stays, planting a garden over the old temple's debt-records. Emotional beat: the smuggler learns to belong without a transaction.

chapters.title: The First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Epilogue. A child brings Kestrel a prayer, and for the first time Kestrel answers it herself—not as a god, but as a person with a little divinity and a lot of stubbornness. Emotional beat: resolution; the valley is no longer a hollow, and neither is she.
